newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD ready to continue tax talks regardless of coal.
newsitem.headline: SPD ready to continue tax talks regardless of coal.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) said on Wednesday they were ready to continue talks with the government on tax reform, regardless of the outcome of crisis talks between Bonn and the mining union.
The SPD boycotted the tax talks last week after the government announced massive cuts in the subsidies it planned to pay to the ailing mining sector.

Since then the SPD, whose cooperation Chancellor Helmut Kohl needs for a comprehensive tax reform programme, has said it will wait to see what Kohl offers the miners in talks now postponed until Thursday.

But SPD party manager Franz Muentefering replied "Yes, of course" when asked on German Radio whether the SPD would return to the tax talks even if it was not satisfied with Kohl's offer to the miners.
"We are committed to help the miners but we are also committed to help other unemployed workers including those who are currently demonstrating in the construction industry," he said.
At the same time he urged the government to make an offer to the miners which meant there would not have to be any forced layoffs among the 90,000 miners between now and 2005.
He said this would require an annual subsidy level of between 6.5 and seven billion marks, compared to the gradual decline to 3.5 billion marks by 2005 that Bonn is proposing.
